whisper.text:
Pete Regina takes us into the physics of holography with this lecture presented at the Hollow
Centre Summer Museum on Governors Island in 2014.
Pete Regina is going to be doing a workshop on the physics of holography and he's been
doing this workshop for quite a while.
I'm really excited to see what he's got to tell us.
All right, thank you everybody.
The whole quick review that I'm going to do here are four basic things.
Four basic things that are pretty simple in their own right, but they kind of come together
in a non-obvious way to really show how holography works and why it works.
What we've been watching on TV on the screen here is some of Rudy Burkow's work.
Rudy, amazing holographer, did very pioneering work in the areas of color holography and
also using holographic elements.

He's been doing a lot of work on holography and holographic elements as objects for holograms.
I'll talk a little bit about that as we get into the setting, but I definitely want to
credit him and all that stuff.
I'll talk about what's a hologram, what is a hologram, what are we talking about, the
four elements I mentioned before, and then I'll talk about some setups and color and
various things at the end.
Again, if you have any questions, just let me know.
What is a hologram?
